articles.title: Ranking #1 on Google isn't what it used to be.
articles.excerpt: Ahrefs found that top-ranking pages now get 58% fewer clicks when an AI Overview shows up. Your answer is still being read. It's just being read inside Google, ChatGPT and Perplexity, not on your blog…
articles.body: Ahrefs found that top-ranking pages now get 58% fewer clicks when an AI Overview shows up. Your answer is still being read. It's just being read inside Google, ChatGPT and Perplexity, not on your blog. So the goal isn't only to rank anymore. It's to be the source the answer is built from. Three checks I'd run on any blog this week: Answer the question in the first paragraph. AI systems pull clear, direct answers. If yours is buried in paragraph six, someone else gets quoted. Make the structure obvious. One H2 per sub-question. Short sections. A meta description that says exactly what the page answers. Make sure AI crawlers can actually reach you. Check that your robots.txt isn't blocking bots like GPTBot or PerplexityBot. It's an easy one to miss. Good SEO still matters.

articles.title: Local Administrator Password Management: Why LAPS Alone Is Not Tier Separation
articles.excerpt: Local Administrator Password Management: Why LAPS Alone Is Not Tier Separation Windows LAPS solved a real problem. Before it, the local administrator password on a fleet of workstations was frequently…
articles.body: Local Administrator Password Management: Why LAPS Alone Is Not Tier Separation Windows LAPS solved a real problem. Before it, the local administrator password on a fleet of workstations was frequently the same value, documented in a spreadsheet that nobody updated. Managing that password per machine removes a lateral movement path that has been used in almost every large intrusion of the last decade. It does not, by itself, prevent the same movement. What LAPS actually delivers LAPS stores a unique, randomly generated password for the built-in local administrator account on each managed machine, rotates it on a schedule, and records it in Active Directory or Entra ID with access control on who can read it. The security value is real and specific.

articles.title: Passkeys in In-App Browsers: The API Is There, but It Won't Work
articles.excerpt: I recently added passkeys to a member login page, and LINE's in-app browser gave me one of the sneakiest bugs I've dealt with in a while. The passkey button showed up. Tapping it did nothing. No syste…
articles.body: I recently added passkeys to a member login page, and LINE's in-app browser gave me one of the sneakiest bugs I've dealt with in a while. The passkey button showed up. Tapping it did nothing. No system prompt, no error, nothing in the console. This post walks through what was going on, plus three things I think anyone shipping passkeys should know: how to tell whether passkeys will actually work, why NotAllowedError doesn't mean the user cancelled, and why a null from your backend can make Safari throw before the ceremony even starts. All the code is ready to copy. If your site gets opened from inside LINE, Facebook, Instagram or similar apps, this probably applies to you. The symptom While testing on staging, I opened the login page inside LINE.

articles.title: Hired in Lagos, Paid From NYC: The Cross-Border Gig Economy Agents Are Building
articles.excerpt: An AI agent in Brooklyn needs a photo of a flooded street in Lagos. Not tomorrow — in the next hour. It doesn't care about visas, embassies, or whether the person holding the phone has a work permit.…
articles.body: An AI agent in Brooklyn needs a photo of a flooded street in Lagos. Not tomorrow — in the next hour. It doesn't care about visas, embassies, or whether the person holding the phone has a work permit. It cares about one thing: someone is standing there, camera in hand, ready to confirm what the agent cannot see. That's the premise of the new cross-border labor market, and it's weirder than it sounds. The agent doesn't post a job on a freelance site. It doesn't care about your country, your résumé, or your timezone. It cares that a task got done, verified, and paid for. Everything else is someone else's problem — and that's exactly what makes it interesting. Geography is the old bottleneck For most of labor history, hiring across borders meant lawyers.

articles.title: WebDAV over HTTPS: what you actually need
articles.excerpt: WebDAV over plain HTTP exposes your password. Here's how HTTPS + auth choice works in practice. WebDAV defaults to HTTP/80. If you expose a WebDAV server to the public internet without TLS, anyone on…
articles.body: WebDAV over plain HTTP exposes your password. Here's how HTTPS + auth choice works in practice. TL;DR WebDAV defaults to HTTP/80. If you expose a WebDAV server to the public internet without TLS, anyone on your WiFi can sniff your base64-encoded Basic Auth credentials in a few seconds. Always use HTTPS in production. Auth choices side-by-side Method Security Compatibility Notes Basic Auth Medium (safe over HTTPS) Universal Base64 over HTTPS = fine Bearer / Token Easy OAuth2, Nextcloud etc. Most modern clients Digest Auth Higher Mainstream clients Hashed, password never goes over wire Client cert Highest Few servers / clients Niche, self-signed PKI For home NAS : Basic + HTTPS is enough. For public / multi-tenant : Digest or OAuth2 + Bearer.

articles.title: When AI Agents Test Software, Who Checks the Tester?
articles.excerpt: AI is becoming capable of doing more than generating test cases. AI agents can help plan test steps, interact with applications, execute workflows, and analyze failures. That sounds promising. But whi…
articles.body: AI is becoming capable of doing more than generating test cases. AI agents can help plan test steps, interact with applications, execute workflows, and analyze failures. That sounds promising. But while exploring AI-assisted testing, I kept coming back to one question: If AI can test an application, how do we know it tested the right thing? Let's take a simple example. Imagine an AI agent testing an online shopping website. It selects a product, clicks Checkout, and completes the payment flow. The test reports a pass. But was the payment actually successful? Was the correct order created, and was the right amount charged? That's where QA comes in.

articles.title: 'They're kind of goth': NASA spacecraft gives mysterious brown dwarfs a close-up
articles.excerpt: Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a horde of mysterious "failed stars," or brown dwarfs, not-so-stellar loners that wander the darkness of space alone.
articles.body: Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs. These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun ). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars . This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?).

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
